questions.q: An unconscious casualty may have a neck injury and needs their airway cleared. What matters more?
options: Keeping the neck still: the airway can wait until the ambulance arrives
First find and fit a collar, then deal with breathing
Do not touch anything: any movement could damage the spinal cord
The airway: opening it matters more than keeping the neck still
questions.explain: Without breathing, a person will die within minutes, so opening the airway matters more than keeping the neck still ⟦18⟧. Do this gently, trying to keep the neck in a neutral position.

questions.q: A casualty with back pain, very agitated, is trying to get up. Persuasion is not working. What should you do?
options: Calmly keep asking them not to move, but do not hold them down by force
Hold them down by force, pinning their shoulders to the ground until the ambulance arrives
Help them quickly get up and walk a little, since that is what they want
Sternly threaten to leave if they do not lie still
questions.explain: Ask the person to stay still, but never force them into a particular position: struggling can make the injury worse ⟦19⟧. Speak calmly and explain why it is important not to move.

questions.q: A casualty has a heavily bleeding wound on the forearm. What should you do first?
options: Press firmly and continuously on the wound through clean cloth or a dressing
Remove the clothing from the wound and examine how deep the cut is
Apply a tourniquet to the upper arm straight away, without even trying to press on the wound
Cover the wound with salt or sugar to make the blood clot faster
questions.explain: The first and main way to stop severe bleeding is firm direct pressure on the wound ⟦20⟧. A tourniquet is needed only if bleeding from a limb is life-threatening and cannot be stopped with pressure.

questions.q: The dressing you are pressing onto the wound has soaked through. What should you do?
options: Remove it, quickly examine the wound, and press on a new dressing
Stop pressing: the blood will clot by itself under the wet dressing
Do not remove it: put another one on top and keep pressing firmly
Remove the dressing and apply a tourniquet, even if the wound is on the stomach
questions.explain: Do not remove a soaked-through dressing: this can dislodge the clot that has started to form. Put more cloth on top and keep pressing firmly (American Red Cross). A tourniquet is applied only to an arm or a leg ⟦21⟧.

questions.q: A tourniquet was applied 40 minutes ago, and the ambulance is still on its way. A relative suggests loosening the tourniquet “to let the leg rest”. What should you do?
options: Loosen it for a couple of minutes, then tighten it again
Remove it completely: after 40 minutes, the tourniquet is already more dangerous than the wound
Move the tourniquet below the wound, so the leg does not go numb
Do not loosen or remove it: only medics do this
questions.explain: Once applied, a tourniquet is not loosened or removed: only medics remove it ⟦22⟧. The time it was applied must be recorded and reported to the crew.

questions.q: For what kind of bleeding is a tourniquet used?
options: For any bleeding from an arm or leg, straight away, even before pressing on the wound
For life-threatening bleeding from an arm or leg, if pressure does not help
For severe nosebleeds, if they do not stop within 10-15 minutes
For any severe bleeding, including from a wound on the stomach or neck
questions.explain: A tourniquet is a device for limbs. It is applied for life-threatening bleeding from an arm or leg, if direct pressure does not help: 5-7 cm above the wound, and not over a joint ⟦23⟧.

questions.q: A piece of metal is sticking out of a wound on the thigh. What should you do?
options: Quickly pull it out and immediately press firmly on the wound with clean cloth
Do not remove it: pad around it with rolls of cloth and press around it
Cut off the protruding part level with the skin and bandage the leg
Apply a tight pressure dressing directly over the fragment and the wound
questions.explain: An embedded object may itself be blocking a damaged blood vessel, and removing it will make the bleeding worse. It is not removed - instead, pad around it with soft rolls of cloth and press around the edges, not on the object itself (Highway Code UK, Annex 7).

questions.q: Which of these is part of the first aid kit contents approved by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Kazakhstan, and helps to stop severe bleeding?
options: Painkiller tablets and cotton wool
Smelling salts and validol
A cervical collar and a splint
A tourniquet and gauze bandages
questions.explain: Under the contents set by the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Kazakhstan, the first aid kit contains a tourniquet, sterile and non-sterile bandages, a dressing pack, plasters, gloves, scissors, a resuscitation face shield and a survival blanket. There are no medicines, smelling salts, cervical collar or splint in this list.
questions.ref: First aid kit contents (Order of the Ministry of Health of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 118/2020); List of Defects, para. 38

questions.q: A driver burned their hand an hour ago and has done nothing since. Is there any point cooling the burn now?
options: No: cooling only helps in the first 5 minutes after a burn
No: after an hour, a burn should only be treated with oil or cream
Yes: cooling with water helps if you start within 3 hours
Yes, but only with ice now, otherwise the burn will not cool down
questions.explain: Cool a burn with cool running water for at least 20 minutes. This can help even if started within 3 hours of the burn, but the sooner the better (ANZCOR 9.1.3).

questions.q: It is winter, water is scarce, but there is plenty of snow around. Can you put snow or ice on a burn?
options: No: ice and snow damage tissue - you need cool water
Yes: snow is clean, and the burn will cool faster than under water
Yes, if you wrap the ice in cloth and hold it there for about an hour
Yes, but only for a small burn on the face or fingers
questions.explain: Ice and icy water cause additional tissue damage (ANZCOR 9.1.3). Cool the burn with cool running water, and if there is little available, use what you have, and keep the person from becoming too cold.

questions.q: Blisters have formed at the site of a burn. What should you do?
options: Prick them with a clean needle and let the fluid out
Cut off the skin of the blister with scissors from the first aid kit
Do not open the blisters, and loosely cover the burn
Cauterise them with alcohol and bandage tightly
questions.explain: Blisters are not pricked or cut off: the skin over them protects the burn from infection (ANZCOR 9.1.3). Cool the burn, then loosely cover it with a clean material.

questions.q: Clothing has stuck to the burnt skin, and there are rings on the fingers. What should you do?
options: Do not pull off the stuck fabric, but carefully remove the rings and watch
Quickly rip off the stuck clothing while the burn is still fresh
Do not remove anything, not even the rings: this will be done at the hospital
Rub everything with oil to make it easier to remove the clothing and rings
questions.explain: Stuck clothing is not pulled off, so as not to tear the skin. Rings, watches and tight items are removed straight away: burnt tissue swells, and jewellery will start to constrict the finger or hand (ANZCOR 9.1.3).

questions.q: A burn has been cooled for 20 minutes. What should you cover it with?
options: Pack it with a thick layer of cotton wool and bandage it tightly
Loosely apply cling film or a non-stick dressing
Rub in burn cream and bandage it fairly tightly
Nothing: let the burn dry out in the air and form a scab
questions.explain: Cotton wool sticks to the wound. Loosely cover the burn with cling film or a clean non-stick dressing. Lay the film along the limb rather than wrapping it around, since the limb will swell (ANZCOR 9.1.3).

questions.q: You are cooling a large burn on someone's leg with water, and they start shivering from the cold. What should you do?
options: Stop cooling and rub the leg to warm it up
Give them a little alcohol to drink to warm up from the inside
Pack the burn with snow instead of water, and wrap up the body
Cool only the burn, and cover the rest of the body
questions.explain: With large burns, it is easy to make the person too cold. Cool only the burnt area, and cover the rest of the body to keep them warm (ANZCOR 9.1.3).

questions.q: Someone's clothing has caught fire. What should you do?
options: Let them run to the nearest water and jump in
Do not let them run: lay them down, cover them with heavy cloth, and roll them over
Wave a jacket at the flames to blow the fire out with a rush of air
Let them stand still and beat out the flames with their hands while you look for water
questions.explain: Running makes the flames burn more fiercely. Stop the person, lay them down, cover them with heavy cloth and roll them along the ground, then cool the burn with water (ANZCOR 9.1.3).

questions.q: Electrolyte from a broken battery has splashed onto someone's hand. What should you do?
options: Wipe it off with a dry cloth and do nothing more
Sprinkle on baking soda to neutralise the acid, and do not rinse it off
Rinse it immediately under running water for at least 20 minutes
Apply a thick cream to protect the skin from the acid
questions.explain: A chemical burn is rinsed immediately under running water for at least 20 minutes, to wash away the acid (ANZCOR 9.1.3). Baking soda or cream will not replace rinsing, and will only waste time.

questions.q: A casualty has an open fracture of the shin: bone is visible in the wound. What should you do?
options: Do not touch the bone, cover the wound with a clean dressing, and immobilise the leg
Carefully push the bone back into place, then apply a tight dressing
Push the bone back inside the wound and bandage the leg tightly
Ask the casualty to move their leg to check for a fracture
questions.explain: The bone is not set, and nothing reaches into the wound, so as not to introduce infection or damage blood vessels. Cover the wound with a clean dressing, and immobilise the leg in the position found (MedlinePlus; First Aid Standard of the Republic of Kazakhstan, para. 8).

questions.q: How should you correctly immobilise a leg with a suspected fracture of the shin?
options: Straighten the leg and tie it to a board only at the site of the fracture
Tightly wrap the injury site with a tourniquet, so it does not swell
Do not immobilise anything, and help the person walk to the car
Without straightening it, splint it above and below the injury site
questions.explain: The leg is not straightened and is immobilised in the position found, supporting the areas both above and below the injury (MedlinePlus; First Aid Standard of the Republic of Kazakhstan, para. 8). Rolled-up clothing, a board or a rolled-up newspaper will do.

questions.q: Which signs in a casualty after a road accident suggest possible shock?
options: A red face, a slow strong pulse, hot and dry skin
Frequent sneezing, hiccups, itchy skin and red eyes
Pale, cold, clammy skin, a fast weak pulse
A small bruise on the arm and complaints of mild knee pain
questions.explain: Shock is a dangerous disruption of blood supply to the organs, for example due to blood loss. Its signs are pale, cold, clammy skin, a fast weak pulse, shallow breathing, restlessness or confusion (MedlinePlus). Call 112 or 103, stop any bleeding, lay the person down and cover them, and give them nothing to eat or drink.

questions.q: A motorcyclist is conscious and breathing normally after a fall. Does the helmet need to be removed?
options: Yes, straight away, so it is easier for them to breathe and speak
No: a helmet is not removed unless it is needed to save a life
Yes, to examine the head and check for a wound
Yes, but carefully, leaving only the chin strap fastened
questions.explain: Removing a helmet can easily shift the head and injure the neck, so it is removed only if necessary (Highway Code UK, para. 283). If the person is breathing normally, the helmet is left on until the medics arrive, and the motorcyclist should not move their head suddenly.

questions.q: A motorcyclist is unconscious and not breathing normally, with their face covered by the helmet. What should you do?
options: Do not touch the helmet under any circumstances, and wait for the ambulance
Quickly rip off the helmet in one pull, so as not to waste time
Only check the pulse through the jacket collar and wait for the doctors
Remove the helmet with two people: one holds the head and neck, the other slides the helmet off
questions.explain: The helmet is removed only when necessary, for example to open the airway and start resuscitation: the airway matters more than keeping the neck still ⟦24⟧. If possible, this is done by two people: one holds the head and neck, while the other slides the helmet off without twisting it.

questions.q: On which vehicles in Kazakhstan must there be a first aid kit?
options: On passenger cars, trucks, buses, wheeled tractors and motorcycles with a sidecar
Only on buses, taxis and other vehicles that carry passengers for a fare
Only on vehicles that carry children, and on school and city bus routes
On none: in Kazakhstan, having a first aid kit in a vehicle is only a recommendation, not a requirement
questions.explain: Under the List of Defects, it is prohibited to operate a bus, a passenger car, a truck or a wheeled tractor without a first aid kit, a fire extinguisher and a warning triangle. A motorcycle with a sidecar must have a first aid kit and a warning triangle ⟦25⟧.

questions.q: A passenger has choked on food: at first they were coughing, but now they cannot cough or speak. What should you do?
options: Give up to five back blows between the shoulder blades
Give them water to wash the piece down
Try to reach the piece with your fingers, blindly, deep in the throat
Wait for them to cough it up on their own, and do not touch them
questions.explain: While the person is coughing, encourage them to keep coughing. If the cough stops or becomes ineffective, give up to five back blows, then, if needed, up to five abdominal thrusts, and call an ambulance. Do not sweep the throat blindly with your fingers, and if the person loses consciousness, start resuscitation ⟦26⟧.

questions.q: You are involved in a road accident in which someone was injured. What do the Rules require you to do for them?
options: Nothing: only medics and rescuers give help to casualties
Take possible steps to give first aid and call an ambulance
Only take down their details and report them to your insurance company
Wait for the police and only approach the casualty with their permission
questions.explain: A driver involved in a road accident must take possible steps to give first aid to the injured and call an ambulance. In an emergency, the injured person is sent in a passing vehicle, and if that is not possible, taken to the nearest hospital in the driver's own vehicle.
